items.title: Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA Series
items.author: CISA
items.content:
Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code with webserver privileges.

The following versions of Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA Series are affected:

  • AK-SM8xxA <=5.4.0 (CVE-2026-129713)
Stack-based Buffer Overflow
  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Commercial Facilities
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: Denmark
A stack-based buffer overflow in an unauthenticated CGI handler of the Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA Series controller allows remote attackers to send specially crafted HTTP/S POST requests, leading to memory corruption, webserver restart and hypothetically potential arbitrary code execution with webserver privileges. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.
Danfoss AK-SM8xxA <=5.4.0

Product Status: known_affected

This vulnerability will be addressed in an upcoming Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series software release (version 5.5.x). In addition, Danfoss will remove the ability for users to disable Strict Mode in future software releases.

Until a software update is available, Danfoss recommends the following mitigations: * Follow the guidance provided in the product documentation and do not expose devices directly to the Internet or assign them public IP addresses. * Restrict remote access to affected devices by using a secure VPN or other protected network architecture. * Configure all affected devices to operate in Strict Mode, which provides enhanced security protections. * Use strong, unique passwords for all user accounts and administrative access. * For additional security recommendations and best practices see the Danfoss AK-SM 800 security guidance page: https://www.danfoss.com/en/service-and-support/downloads/dcs/adap-kool-software/ak-sm-800a/#tab-overview

  • Carlo Meijer of Midnight Blue reported CVE-2026-129713 to CISA.

CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.

  • Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.
  • When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.

CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.

Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.

items.title: AutomationDirect C-More EA9 Programming Software
items.author: CISA
items.content: If you cannot update to the latest software or firmware version right away, apply the following compensating controls to reduce risk until the update can be performed. These measures are temporary and do not replace the update, which remains the primary and recommended remediation. Apply these controls as appropriate based on the vulnerability, assessed risk, operational requirements, and characteristics of your environment. Implement changes under your established management-of-change process. Before implementing isolation, access-control, or network-configuration changes, evaluate potential impacts to safety, availability, and essential operational functions. • Isolate affected engineering workstations and OT systems from external and nonessential networks, including the internet and corporate IT networks, where operationally feasible. • Disable or tightly restrict vendor, contractor, and other remote access to the affected OT environment until the vulnerability can be remediated. Where remote access is operationally required, use a hardened jump host, enforce multi-factor authentication, apply least-privilege access, and limit access to authorized, time-bound sessions. • Use trusted, dedicated OT networks for device communication. Where practicable and appropriate to the assessed risk, use dedicated or physically separated infrastructure for higher-criticality systems. Where logical segmentation is used, ensure segmentation controls are appropriately configured, secured, and monitored. • Restrict both physical and logical access to affected systems to authorized personnel only. Apply least-privilege principles to administrative, engineering, maintenance, and service access. • Configure application allowlisting, where supported, so that only trusted and pre-approved applications are permitted to execute. Block unauthorized software. • Use appropriate antivirus or endpoint detection and response (EDR) tools where supported and compatible with the affected system. Configure host-based and network firewalls to permit only required communications. • Disable unnecessary services, ports, protocols, and communication pathways associated with the affected systems. Where a service or protocol cannot be disabled for operational reasons, restrict access to trusted systems and authorized users wherever possible. • Enable and regularly review available system, security, and network logs to identify suspicious or unauthorized activity. Where appropriate, monitor communications to and from affected systems for unexpected connections or changes in network behavior. • Maintain secure, tested, and preferably offline backups of PLC programs, device configurations, engineering workstation configurations, and other information necessary to restore operations. Periodically verify that backups can be successfully restored. • Verify that critical OT functions can continue operating without unnecessary dependencies on external networks, cloud services, remote-access services, corporate IT services, or other nonessential systems. • If removable media is required to transfer files into an isolated or restricted environment, use controlled and trusted media and scan it for malicious content before use. • Continuously evaluate the risks associated with operating vulnerable or outdated firmware or software. Adjust compensating controls as the threat environment, operational requirements, or available vulnerability information changes. These compensating controls are intended to reduce exposure while remediation is pending. Organizations should prioritize applying the vendor-provided update as soon as it can be safely tested and deployed within the operational environment.

items.author: CISA

items.title: Siemens SIMATIC WinCC
items.author: CISA
items.content:
Graphics Designer of SIMATIC WinCC before V8.2 contains an implicit active content execution vulnerability upon opening files, which could allow an attacker to cause arbitrary code execution on the device. Siemens is preparing fixes and recommends specific mitigations for products where fixes are not or not yet available.

The following versions of Siemens SIMATIC WinCC are affected:

  • SIMATIC WinCC V7.5 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-59082)
  • SIMATIC WinCC V8.0 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-59082)
  • SIMATIC WinCC V8.1 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-59082)
Insufficient UI Warning of Dangerous Operations
  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: Germany
Affected devices implicitly execute active content when opening files. This could allow an attacker to make the user execute arbitrary code on the device.

Product Status: known_affected

The affected product may be operated only by personnel qualified for the specific task in accordance with the relevant documentation, in particular its warning notices and safety instructions. Qualified personnel are those who, based on their training and experience, are capable of identifying risks and avoiding potential hazards when working with the affected product. Also make sure to only open files from trusted sources.

Siemens has released new versions for the affected products and recommends to update to the latest versions.

The following versions of Siemens Mendix SAML Module are affected:

  • Mendix SAML (Mendix 10 compatible) vers:intdot/<4.2.4 (CVE-2026-89209)
  • Mendix SAML (Mendix 11 compatible) vers:intdot/<4.2.4 (CVE-2026-89209)
  • Mendix SAML (Mendix 9 compatible) vers:intdot/<3.6.29 (CVE-2026-89209)
Mendix SAML (Mendix 10 compatible)
Authentication Bypass by Capture-replay
  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Information Technology
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: Germany
Affected versions of the module do not properly protect against SAML assertion replay in IdP-initiated authentication flows. This could allow unauthenticated remote attackers to gain unauthorized access to the application by replaying a valid SAML response.
Mendix SAML (Mendix 10 compatible) < V4.2.4

Product Status: known_affected

Disable IdP-initiated SSO

Update to V4.2.4 or later version

Mendix SAML (Mendix 11 compatible) < V4.2.4

Product Status: known_affected

Disable IdP-initiated SSO

Update to V4.2.4 or later version

Mendix SAML (Mendix 9 compatible) < V3.6.29

Product Status: known_affected

Disable IdP-initiated SSO

Update to V3.6.29 or later version

As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (Download: https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurity

For further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisories

The use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use.

CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.

  • Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.
  • When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.

CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.

items.title: Hitachi Energy CoreTec Product
items.author: CISA
items.content:
Hitachi Energy is aware of OS command injection and Dirty Frag vulnerabilities that affect CoreTec product versions listed in this document. Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could result in impact on confidentiality, integrity and availability of the product. Please refer to the Recommended Immediate Actions for information about the mitigation/remediation.

The following versions of Hitachi Energy CoreTec Product are affected:

  • CoreTec5 vers:CoreTec5/<=3.4.0, 5.0.0 (CVE-2026-13162, CVE-2026-43284)
  • CoreTec4 vers:CoreTec4/<=3.4.0 (CVE-2026-13162)
Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection'), Write-what-where Condition
  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Energy
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: Switzerland
An OS command vulnerability exists in CoreTec product that allows authenticated users with certain roles to execute arbitrary system commands with full control over the device. The vulnerability exists in the configuration daemon's time synchronization handler, which is responsible for setting the system timezone. When processing timezone configuration updates, the daemon constructs a shell command by concatenating user-supplied input without any sanitization or validation.
CoreTec5 versions 3.4.0 and prior

Product Status: fixed, known_affected, recommended

Update to CoreTec5 version 5.0.0

CoreTec4 versions 3.4.0 and prior

Product Status: fixed, known_affected, recommended

Upgrade to CoreTec5 version 5.0.0

Follow general mitigation factors

A vulnerability exists in the IPsec ESP subsystem (esp4) of the Linux kernel used in CoreTec5 that allows a local unprivileged user to escalate privileges to root. The flaw exists in how the kernel handles memory pages when processing ESP encrypted network packets. An attacker can craft a packet that causes the kernel to decrypt data directly into memory pages it does not own, including cached copies of privileged operating system binaries. When one of those binaries is executed, the attacker's injected code runs with root privileges. In CoreTec5, the vulnerable ESP component is compiled in kernel as a built-in and is present at boot time allowing a local user to exploit it.
CoreTec5 versions 3.4.0 and prior

Product Status: fixed, known_affected, recommended

Update to CoreTec5 version 5.0.0

CoreTec4 versions 3.4.0 and prior

Product Status: fixed, known_affected, recommended

CoreTec5 versions 3.4.0 and prior

Product Status: fixed, known_affected, recommended

Update to CoreTec5 version 5.0.0

items.author: CISA
items.content:
Hitachi Energy is aware of multiple vulnerabilities that affect the TRO600 series product versions listed in this document. These vulnerabilities can be exploited for remote code execution (RCE) to carry out further attacks and disclosure of sensitive information. Please refer to the Recommended Immediate Actions section for information about the mitigation/remediation.

The following versions of Hitachi Energy TRO600 series products are affected:

  • TRO600 vers:TRO600/<=9.2.1.6, vers:TRO600/<=9.1.1.0, 9.2.2.1, 9.1.2.0 (CVE-2026-10756, CVE-2026-106087)
Improper Restriction of Communication Channel to Intended Endpoints, Missing Authentication for Critical Function
  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Energy
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: Switzerland
TRO600 contains a vulnerability that allows an authenticated attacker to bypass network access restrictions and access services intended to be reachable only from localhost. By leveraging port forwarding, an attacker can interact with locally bound ports and services, resulting in unauthorized access to sensitive functionality and confidential information, and causing availability impact.
TRO600 version 9.2.1.6 and prior

Product Status: fixed, known_affected, recommended

Update to version 9.2.2.1

TRO600 contains an arbitrary file read vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker can exploit this vulnerability to read or download arbitrary files on the affected device, including sensitive configuration files and password data, resulting in the disclosure of sensitive information.
TRO600 version 9.2.1.6 and prior

Product Status: fixed, known_affected, recommended
